subject: DPA escalation roles & remediation playbook review
body:
From: Susan Ross <susan.ross@acme.com>

Cc: security@acme-inc.com

Subject: Question: notification window and cooperation expectations under our DPA

Hi Aditya,

We had an internal tabletop this morning and Acme's legal/security team wants clarity on Redwood's commitments under Section 7 (Incident Notification) of our DPA. Specifically:

- Our standard says controller must be notified "without undue delay" but the Acme SOC team wants an explicit operational window (they suggested 24 hours for initial notice).
- They also want to understand detail on evidence preservation, log retention, and the level of forensic cooperation Redwood will provide (e.g., full request for logs, timeline artifacts, and file-level indicators).
- Finally, they asked whether Redwood will coordinate public/partner/customer communications or whether they must own that entirely.

Can you confirm our preferred position and whether we can agree to a 24-hour initial notification? I've attached our DPA excerpt and flagged the clause.

Thanks,
Susan
Security Program Manager
Acme Payments

Thanks for the ping. Quick thoughts:

- Contract/Legal stance: We should avoid a hard 24-hour commitment. Under GDPR and typical processor-controller constructs we commit to "without undue delay" plus an operational practice; many vendors use a 48-hour initial notice once we have a confirmed incident that meets the DPA's breach definition.
- Evidence & logs: We can commit to preserving relevant logs and a forensic snapshot for a defined retention (we currently keep request/trace logs 90 days, and can extract a forensic bundle on request). We should be explicit about what we can provide (e.g., request traces, ingest logs, stored object metadata) vs. what we cannot (customer PII copies we don't retain beyond controller stores).
- Communications: We can offer to coordinate messaging (review drafts, share timelines, provide technical summaries) but recommend the controller lead any customer-facing notices. Joint messaging for joint incidents is acceptable with clear timelines/approvals.

I'm attaching a short redline suggestion for the DPA language (playbook references included). I don't want to promise a 24h SLA without ops/legal buy-in.

Monica
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

-----Reply (technical)-----
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Question: notification window and cooperation expectations under our DPA

FYI from infra: from an engineering standpoint we can meet a 48-hour initial notification window for incidents where the service shows evidence of unauthorized access. However, the initial triage timeline depends on detection — we can send a preliminary status update within 24 hours of detection if the detection team flags it as high-severity, but we should avoid committing to it universally.

On artifacts: we can produce request trace bundles, host-level metrics, and KV-cache snapshots. Full forensic disk images require more time and may need a preservation hold. We should set expectations that some artifacts require escalation and legal approval (and potentially Law enforcement subpoena) to preserve.

Markus
Principal Infra Engineer

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Proposed reply to Acme (draft):

"Hi Susan — thanks for raising these important questions. Redwood treats data incidents with high priority and seeks to partner closely with customers. Our proposed approach: we will provide an initial incident notification to the controller as soon as we confirm an incident that meets the DPA breach definition; operationally we aim to send a preliminary status update within 48 hours of confirmation and a more detailed technical report within 5 business days. Redwood will preserve relevant logs and artifacts for 90 days and will provide request traces, timeline artifacts, and a forensic summary upon request. We are happy to review and comment on customer-facing communications and coordinate messaging, while recognizing the controller typically leads external notifications. Where required, Redwood will cooperate with regulatory or law enforcement requests per the DPA and applicable law."

Lauren suggests we offer 48h preliminary and 5-business-day detailed report. Thoughts?

Lauren

Subject: Re: Question: notification window and cooperation expectations under our DPA

Hi Susan — appreciate the clear asks. Apologies for the delay while we looped in legal and engineering; below is Redwood's operational position that we can commit to today for inclusion in our DPA redlines or an SOW addendum.

Operational position (proposed):
- Initial notification: Redwood will notify the controller without undue delay upon confirmation that an event meets the DPA breach definition. Operationally, Redwood aims to provide a preliminary status update within 48 hours of confirmation.
- Detailed report: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to deliver a detailed technical report within 5 business days of confirmation; timing may vary with incident complexity.
- Evidence & preservation: Redwood will preserve relevant logs and create a forensic bundle on request. Preserved artifacts include request traces, ingest/ingress logs, metadata for stored objects, and timeline artifacts. Redwood retains primary telemetry and request logs for 90 days by default. For preservation beyond 90 days or for full disk images, Redwood will require a preservation request and may need legal process.
- Communications: Redwood will coordinate message drafts and technical summaries and prefers the controller to lead customer-facing communications. For joint public notices Redwood will request review/approval windows (typical 24–48 hours) before posting.
- Escalation contacts: security@redwood.ai (security triage), legal@redwood.ai (legal / DPA questions), lauren_bishop@redwood.ai (customer liaison).

If this reads OK I'll send a short redline to Section 7 and attach the playbook excerpt. Happy to adjust the 48-hour operational aim if Acme needs a stricter SLA, but legal is reluctant to hard-commit to 24 hours across all incident classes.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
